claim_text: Serial ddPCR in two patients showed Q859K, and in one case W780R, emerging with rebound of the founder H1047R mutation and preceding or accompanying radiographic progression `pmid-37916958`.
evidence_summary: The paper reports serial ctDNA ddPCR in two patients with acquired mutations at progression to inavolisib. In both patients, cleared PIK3CA H1047R later rebounded before radiographic progression, accompanied by Q859K; patient 4643 also developed W780R and AKT1 mutations, while patient 2542 mutations remained detectable through progression and autopsy.

claim_text: Downstream signaling assays similarly showed reduced potency of alpelisib and inavolisib against the double mutants `pmid-37916958`.
evidence_summary: The paper engineered PIK3CA-mutant T47D and MCF7 models with W780R or Q859H/K double mutants. It states that both inavolisib and alpelisib had reduced potency for downstream signaling inhibition in the presence of W780R or Q859H/K, while RLY-2608 signaling inhibition was unaffected.

claim_text: However, the same paper found co-emergent AKT1 mutations in some resistant patients and showed that engineered AKT1 E17K or Q79K increased resistance to alpelisib and inavolisib while retaining sensitivity to ipatasertib, so allosteric PI3K-alpha inhibition should not be framed as a universal solution for every convergent PI3K-pathway resistance state `pmid-37916958`.
evidence_summary: The study identified AKT1 E17K and other AKT1 mutations emerging with resistance in patient ctDNA/autopsy samples. T47D cells expressing AKT1 E17K or Q79K had increased IC50 values for alpelisib and inavolisib relative to AKT1 wild type, whereas ipatasertib activity was not affected, supporting the caveat that PI3K-alpha allosteric inhibition addresses specific PIK3CA-pocket resistance but not all downstream AKT-mediated states.

claim_text: C-terminal PIK3CA frameshift mutations increased PI3K effector signaling and transformation but remained sensitive to p110-alpha inhibition by alpelisib in cells and xenografts `pmid-32929011`.
evidence_summary: The paper characterizes C-terminal PIK3CA frameshifts as oncogenic, with increased PI3K effector signaling, soft agar growth, transformation, and xenograft tumor growth. It reports p110-alpha-selective pharmacologic inhibition blocked transformation and that breast cell lines and tumors expressing frameshift mutants were sensitive to alpelisib treatment.

claim_text: Second, baseline multiple PIK3CA mutations may mark deeper PI3K dependence rather than acquired resistance: in SANDPIPER ctDNA, clonal multiple PIK3CA mutations correlated with higher response and longer progression-free survival on taselisib plus fulvestrant than subclonal multiple PIK3CA mutations, consistent with prior in-cis double-mutant sensitivity models `pmid-37101291`.
evidence_summary: The SANDPIPER baseline ctDNA analysis reports that clonal multiple PIK3CA-mutant ctDNA samples had fewer RTK or non-PIK3CA PI3K pathway co-alterations, indicating stronger PI3K reliance, and that patients with clonal multiple PIK3CA mutations had significantly higher response rate and longer progression-free survival than those with subclonal multiple PIK3CA mutations. The paper frames this in relation to preclinical double-mutant sensitivity.
